subject: Follow-up: Clarifying where prompt inputs and generated text are stored (PII controls)
messages:
From: Angela Park <angela@healthsync.io>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: security@healthsync.io
Date: 2026-10-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Questions after today's call — storage/retention for prompt data

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the call this morning — good overview. Our security team asked that I get a concise, written summary of how Redwood treats prompt inputs and generated outputs (specifically any PII handling). Could you please confirm the following items so we can include them in our vendor review?

1) What exactly is stored by default (raw prompt text, model-generated text, logs, KV cache snapshots)?
2) Where is that data stored geographically for the hosted service (regions/availability zones)?
3) What are the default retention windows for request/response logs and any cached state?
4) Who at Redwood can access request/response logs by default — is access audited?
5) Does Redwood apply any automatic PII filtering or token redaction for logs? If so, what classes of PII are handled and what is the false-positive/negative expectation?
6) Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS) and, if so, for which deployment modes?
7) For Dedicated or Private deployments, what options are available for zero-retention / no-logging configurations?
8) Any SOC2 / ISO artifacts or a short compliance pointer we can provide to our reviewers.

Attached is the prospect security questionnaire we started (MAV-ProspectSecurityQ.pdf). Happy to take a short follow-up call next week.

Best,
Angela
Angela Park
Head of Platform Security, HealthSync
angela@healthsync.io


From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-12T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions after today's call — storage/retention for prompt data

Hi Angela — thanks for the clear list. Quick recap below and I’ve looped in our security lead, Karthik, for technical confirmation and any caveats. Attached is a one-page post-call summary for the internal buying team (lauren_postcall_summary.docx).

Recap / initial answers (high level):
- Default stored artifacts: request metadata + request/response logs for troubleshooting. We do not persist full KV caches to long-term storage by default.
- Regions: hosted service stores logs in the tenant region (we can pin to US-East, EU-West, or APAC regions depending on your account).
- Retention: default is 14 days for hosted troubleshooting logs; enterprise/Dedicated can change via contract.
- Access: access is role-based, audited, and requires justification (internal access is limited to SRE/support with 2FA + approval).
- PII: we have an automated redaction layer for high-confidence SSN/credit-card/email/phone patterns in logs; more comprehensive PII masking is available as an opt-in eval.
- KMS: BYOK/customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports managed keys but enterprise customers can request KMS integration.
- Zero-retention: Dedicated/Private can be configured for zero or near-zero retention; we’ll confirm exact steps.
- Compliance: Karthik will point to SOC 2 artifacts and the compliance page.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik to confirm technical specifics and any dataflow diagrams we should share.
2) Agree on an NDA/DocuSign link if HealthSync needs artifacts sent under NDA.
3) Book a 30m follow-up with security vs. Karthik + me next week.

If that works, Karthik — can you confirm the retention options and exact defaults in writing?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
(Attachment: lauren_postcall_summary.docx)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Angela Park <angela@healthsync.io>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-14T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions after today's call — storage/retention for prompt data (technical confirmation)

Hi Angela / Lauren — thanks, and sorry for the slight delay. Below are concrete answers and configuration options for HealthSync's reviewer. I’ve attached our data-handling slide deck for reference (redwood-data-handling-slides.pdf).

1) What is stored by default
- Hosted API (default tenant): we persist request metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts) and request/response text logs for debugging. The default debug-log retention window is 14 days.
- KV cache: ephemeral in-memory KV used during generation sessions; these are not written to long-term storage unless you enable a persistent session flag.
- Embeddings & indexes: we do not automatically persist embeddings derived from customer prompts unless explicitly configured by the customer (e.g., vector DB export).

2) Geographic residency
- For hosted accounts, logs are stored in the region of record for the tenant: us-east-1 (US), eu-west-1 (EU), ap-southeast-1 (APAC). We can pin HealthSync’s tenant to us-east-1 as requested.

3) Retention windows (defaults & options)
- Hosted (self-serve): default 14 days for request/response logs; can be reduced to 0 (no retention) via tenant-level privacy toggle (note: reducing to 0 disables request replay/debug features).
- Dedicated (reserved): configurable retention by contract: options include 0, 7, 30, 90, 365, or custom up to 730 days.
- Private/on-prem: retention controlled entirely by the customer (we provide guidance; no Redwood-hosted logs).

4) Access and auditability
- Access is strictly role-based. Internal SRE/support access requires a documented ticket, manager approval, and is time-boxed. All access to request/response logs is recorded in an immutable audit trail (who, why, job id, timestamp). Audit logs are available to customers on Dedicated/Private and can be exported via secure bucket.

5) PII filtering and redaction
- We run a multi-tier pipeline for log hygiene: (a) deterministic pattern detection (SSN, credit-card, email, phone), (b) model-assisted entity recognition to surface likely PII, (c) configurable mask rules customers can add. Deterministic rules have very high precision for common numeric patterns; model-assisted detection reduces false negatives for free-text names/addresses but may introduce false positives — we recommend a review step.
- Redaction behavior: by default we mask high-confidence detections in debug logs. For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide an option to redact at ingestion (preventing raw storage entirely).

6) Encryption & keys
- Transport: TLS 1.3 everywhere.
- At rest: AES-256. Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). BYOK is available during onboarding.

7) Zero-retention and contractual guarantees
- For HealthSync: if you require a contractual zero-retention for hosted traffic, we can offer a dedicated tokenization path (requests are ingested, tokenized, and ephemeral logs are discarded). That path trades off some debug capabilities and streaming traces.

8) Compliance artifacts
- SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA. Our public compliance page is here: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/llm-data-handling (see sections on data retention & keys).

Operational notes / recommended next steps for HealthSync
- If you want to minimize PII risk quickly: enable tenant-level log reduction to 0 and request a Dedicated evaluation with BYOK.
- If you need automatic redaction tuned: we can pilot the advanced PII masking on a sample prompt set and provide a short report on false positives/negatives.

If helpful I can produce a short dataflow diagram showing exactly where each artifact lives and who can pull it.

-Karthik Iyer
Security & Compliance Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
(Attachment: redwood-data-handling-slides.pdf)
